article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 65% Indica / 35% Sativa
Genetics: Ghost of Von Humboldt OG × Caramel Cream × Humboldt Frost
Breeder: Humboldt Seed Company
THC Content: 25–30%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Jet fuel, diesel, Kush, wet-paint funk
Flowering Time (Indoor): Approximately 65 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: October 5 – 20
Indoor Yield: High
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Easy to intermediate

Notorious THC was bred with very little interest in subtlety. Humboldt Seed Company set out to emphasize potency while preserving the resin, terpene intensity, and production qualities expected from premium Humboldt cannabis. The result smells closer to a garage than a bakery: gasoline, diesel fumes, fresh paint, earthy Kush, and chemical resin dominate mature flowers. A faint creamy sweetness may appear beneath the heavier odors, but the overall impression remains aggressively industrial. Thick buds develop beneath a sparkling coat of trichomes, giving the flowers a diamond-dusted appearance that visually reinforces the strain’s reputation for strength.

That potency is not just part of the name. Humboldt lists average THC between 25% and 30%, placing the cultivar comfortably in high-potency territory. The experience can begin with an unusual cerebral lift—talkative, euphoric, imaginative, even philosophical—before the heavier indica character gradually pulls the body toward relaxation and sleepiness. At roughly 65 days indoors, it requires a little more patience than Humboldt’s fastest hybrids, yet the extra flowering time supports very large colas, strong resin development, and high yields. For growers and consumers alike, Notorious THC is built around excess: oversized flowers, loud gas, strong effects, and an unmistakably old-school Kush foundation.
Genetics and Lineage

Humboldt Seed Company lists the parental foundation as Ghost of Von Humboldt OG, Caramel Cream, and Humboldt Frost. Ghost of Von Humboldt OG supplies the deepest Kush influence, contributing fuel, earth, resin, sturdy structure, and the heavy physical character that becomes increasingly noticeable later in the experience. Humboldt Frost reinforces trichome production and gives the finished plant much of the crystalline flower appearance highlighted by the breeder. Caramel Cream adds a softer dimension, introducing creamier sweetness and additional hybrid vigor beneath the otherwise aggressive gas.

Those components produce a cultivar that tastes considerably darker than its Caramel Cream ancestry might suggest. The sweet side does not disappear, but it operates almost like a background note beneath gasoline, paint, pine, and resin. This makes the flower distinct from modern dessert hybrids in which cream or sugar dominates the aromatic identity. Here, the sweeter genetics round off the edges without reducing the intensity of the OG and Frost influence.

Current Humboldt breeder material contains occasional wording variation between “Caramel Cream” in the published parentage field and “California Cream” in portions of the description, while historical breeder-associated records consistently identify Caramel Cream alongside Ghost of Von Humboldt and Humboldt Frost. The commercial cultivar is best understood as that three-part Humboldt breeding project rather than the simplified Humboldt OG × Caramel Cream pedigrees sometimes attached to unrelated commercial flower.
Effects and Experience

The first phase can feel much more cerebral than a 65% indica classification implies. Mood rises quickly, conversation may become easier, and ordinary thoughts can develop unusual depth or significance. Humboldt has long emphasized the cultivar’s mind-bending, philosophical quality, and stronger servings can produce a distinctly introspective experience. Music, films, and long conversations may become absorbing, although detailed concentration often becomes less reliable as intoxication develops.

Physical effects build underneath the mental activity. Shoulders loosen, movement feels increasingly optional, and the initial conversational energy gradually gives way to a deeper state of calm. At moderate amounts, that combination can feel pleasantly social: mentally engaged but physically comfortable. Larger doses shift the balance dramatically toward heaviness, making sleepiness and couch-oriented relaxation much more likely. The transition is one of the strain’s defining characteristics because the early cerebral stage can disguise just how strong the body effects will eventually become.

With THC routinely listed between 25% and 30%, dosage deserves respect. Excessive consumption can cause dizziness, dry mouth, anxiety, disorientation, impaired memory, or uncomfortable sedation. The philosophical reputation should not be interpreted as enhanced objective thinking; THC can impair judgment even when ideas feel unusually interesting or profound. Consumers with limited tolerance should approach a new batch conservatively and allow the full body effect time to develop before consuming more.
Medical Benefits

The gradual change from cerebral euphoria into substantial physical relaxation may interest medical marijuana consumers who prefer an evening-oriented hybrid that does not begin with immediate sedation. Cannabis with comparable effects is sometimes chosen by individuals seeking temporary relief from physical discomfort, appetite changes, or difficulty settling down after daily activity. The later body effect may also appeal to people who find lighter, more stimulating weed insufficiently relaxing.

Notorious THC itself has not been established in controlled clinical trials as a treatment for chronic pain, insomnia, depression, anxiety, or another specific medical condition. Broader cannabinoid research indicates that certain cannabis-based medicines can benefit some patients with chronic pain or nausea, but outcomes vary by product, dose, route of administration, and individual health factors. Those findings should not be converted into strain-specific treatment claims simply because this cultivar is exceptionally potent.

High THC may actually reduce therapeutic usefulness for some individuals. Anxiety, dizziness, impaired coordination, short-term memory disruption, and excessive sleepiness can occur at larger doses, and cannabis may interact with certain medications. Anyone considering marijuana for a medical purpose should use current laboratory information, conservative dosing, and appropriate healthcare guidance rather than treating THC percentage as a direct measure of therapeutic value.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Jet fuel is the clearest reference point. Mature flowers can release a penetrating petroleum aroma almost immediately, followed by diesel, piney Kush, damp earth, and a peculiar chemical sharpness Humboldt compares to fresh paint. That wet-paint quality gives the strain an almost solvent-like edge without becoming identical to the garlic or sulfurous funk found in GMO -derived weed strains . It is a distinctly OG-oriented type of pungency—resinous, fuel-heavy, and earthy.

The flavor becomes broader on the palate. Diesel and Kush tend to lead, followed by woody pine, earth, and a lingering chemical finish. Some expressions reveal mild cream or caramel sweetness after the stronger fuel subsides, likely reflecting the Caramel Cream side of the ancestry. That contrast adds complexity without changing the cultivar into a dessert strain. The strongest examples remain unapologetically gassy from inhale through aftertaste.

Humboldt does not publish one permanent terpene percentage profile for the current seed population. Historical extracts made from this genetic line have shown compounds such as caryophyllene, linalool, humulene, limonene, or nerolidol among prominent terpenes, but concentrate results cannot establish a universal flower profile. Phenotype, cultivation environment, harvest timing, and extraction method can all alter measurable composition. A cool, gradual dry and patient cure help preserve the subtler pine and sweet notes beneath the heavier fuel.
Growing Information

Notorious THC develops into a substantial plant with considerable vertical growth and robust lateral branches. Humboldt describes plants reaching significant height while supporting extremely dense, resinous colas. That architecture creates meaningful yield potential, but large late-flower buds can place considerable mechanical stress on branches. Trellising, stakes, or other forms of support may become useful well before harvest, especially where plants receive long vegetative periods.

Indoor flowering takes up to approximately 65 days. As maturity approaches, trichomes accumulate heavily across the flowers and surrounding surfaces, producing the sparkling appearance central to the strain’s identity. Humboldt rates indoor yields as high without publishing a fixed grams-per-square-meter figure. That is more realistic than attaching one universal number to a seed population, since plant density, root space, lighting, training, environment, and phenotype can alter production substantially.

The breeder describes the cultivar as beginner-friendly, although its size and flower weight still reward basic canopy planning. Indoor gardeners should account for stretch before flowering rather than waiting until large tops approach the lights. Good circulation becomes increasingly important as the colas gain density, and keeping the interior canopy reasonably open helps prevent stagnant pockets of humidity. The plants themselves are vigorous enough to perform in soil or hydroponic systems when environmental conditions remain stable.

Outdoor harvest generally falls between October 5 and October 20. Humboldt rates outdoor yield as high and recommends mild conditions with abundant sunlight for maximum performance. The mid-October finish means local weather matters more than it does with strains harvested in September. Dense, oversized flowers can become vulnerable when prolonged rain, heavy dew, or persistent humidity arrives late in the season, so airflow and weather monitoring become increasingly important as harvest approaches.

Resin is another major cultivation trait. Flowers develop heavy trichome coverage that can make mature buds shine under strong light, and that resinous character has helped the genetics appear in concentrate production as well as premium flower. Gentle harvesting protects those glands, while slow drying allows moisture to leave the thick colas evenly. After curing, the aggressive wet-paint and gasoline aroma usually becomes smoother, allowing the Kush, pine, earth, and mild sweetness to separate more clearly.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Notorious THC?

Humboldt Seed Company lists Notorious THC as a combination of Ghost of Von Humboldt OG, Caramel Cream, and Humboldt Frost. Together, those genetics contribute Kush fuel, creamy undertones, heavy resin, potency, and strong flower production.
Is Notorious THC indica or sativa?
The breeder classifies the cultivar as approximately 65% indica and 35% sativa. The experience can begin cerebral and talkative before becoming significantly more physically relaxing and sleepy.
How strong is Notorious THC?
Humboldt lists average THC between approximately 25% and 30%. Actual potency varies with phenotype, growing conditions, harvest maturity, and laboratory testing.
What does Notorious THC taste like?
The defining profile combines jet fuel, wet paint, diesel, Kush, gas, earth, and pine. Some flowers may reveal subtle creamy or sweet characteristics beneath the stronger fuel notes.
How long does Notorious THC take to flower?
Indoor flowering takes approximately 65 days. Outdoors, Humboldt lists an expected harvest period from roughly October 5 through October 20.
Final Thoughts on Notorious THC

Notorious THC is one of Humboldt Seed Company’s clearest examples of potency being treated as a breeding objective without abandoning aroma or agricultural performance. Ghost of Von Humboldt OG establishes the Kush-heavy foundation, Humboldt Frost reinforces the resin, and Caramel Cream introduces a softer counterpoint beneath the fuel. The finished cultivar can reach 25–30% THC while still producing the kind of complex terpene profile and oversized flowers that prevent it from becoming a numbers-only strain.

Its aroma is arguably even more distinctive than the potency. Gasoline, diesel, wet paint, pine, earth, and Kush create an industrial bouquet far removed from the tropical fruit and candy profiles common in newer cannabis breeding . A touch of cream or sweetness may appear in the background, but fuel remains in control.

Growers receive an equally forceful plant: tall growth, strong branches, dense resinous colas, high yield potential, and a 65-day indoor flowering schedule. Consumers get a high that moves in the opposite direction from many indicas, beginning with cerebral euphoria and conversation before gradually becoming physically heavy and sleepy. Notorious THC ultimately lives up to its name not because potency is its only quality, but because almost every part of the cultivar—from the smell to the flower size to the final body effect—is deliberately larger than life.
